alert.title: Background jobs stalling because Redis keeps refusing writes
alert.symptoms: Order-worker jobs are piling up (backlog over 39k) and Redis is rejecting new writes; memory sits near its limit even though the eviction policy was tuned in the past. Delayed order emails are being reported by support.
alert.error_message: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
alert.log_snippet:
2026-09-28T06:41:00Z ERROR order-worker [redis-client] OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'.
redis_used_memory_pct=99.0% queue_depth=39210 maxmemory_policy=allkeys-lru

response.root_cause: Redis hit its maxmemory limit causing OOM errors and write rejections, likely due to memory‑intensive keys or insufficient maxmemory setting
response.blast_radius: Order‑worker backlog (39k+ jobs), delayed order confirmation emails, potential order fulfillment delays affecting customers and downstream services
first_actions: Inspect Redis memory usage and identify large/expiring keys; consider manual eviction or increasing maxmemory
Temporarily throttle or pause order‑worker job intake to prevent further backlog while Redis is stabilized
Restart Redis with adjusted maxmemory/eviction settings or scale Redis instance, then monitor write health

New alert: Background jobs stalling because Redis keeps refusing writes. Service: order-worker, severity: SEV2.
Symptoms: Order-worker jobs are piling up (backlog over 39k) and Redis is rejecting new writes; memory sits near its limit even though the eviction policy was tuned in the past. Delayed order emails are being reported by support.
Error: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'

Evidence (only these incidents may be cited):
Incident INC-003 (order-worker, SEV2, 2026-05-18T07:05:41Z):
Symptoms: order-worker job processing stalled Monday morning; Redis returning OOM errors, queue depth past 41k, order confirmation emails delayed.
Root cause: Weekend order volume queued jobs and cached idempotency keys in Redis without eviction; by Monday's traffic ramp Redis hit its 2GB maxmemory limit with the default noeviction policy.
Resolver: Ananya Iyer

Incident INC-019 (auth-service, SEV1, 2026-08-11T04:22:37Z):
Symptoms: Users logged out en masse; auth-service session lookups failing with Redis OOM errors starting 04:22 UTC (not a Monday).
Root cause: 'Remember me' sessions were issued with no TTL cap (some over a year old); accumulated session keys filled the auth-service session Redis instance to its 1GB maxmemory limit.
Resolver: Ananya Iyer

Incident INC-008 (order-worker, SEV2, 2026-06-15T06:58:12Z):
Symptoms: Second Monday-morning Redis OOM in a month; order-worker queue depth past 38k again, same signature as INC-003.
Root cause: The allkeys-lru eviction policy set after INC-003 slowed the OOM but idempotency keys from the order-retry-queue still have no TTL, so memory pressure builds back up over the weekend.
Resolver: Ananya Iyer

Ranked fixes (use the top one as first_actions[0]):
  1. restart_redis_and_set_eviction_policy (score=+0.667, worked=1, partial=0, failed=0, recent_failures=0)
  2. manual_flush_stale_keys (score=+0.500, worked=0, partial=2, failed=0, recent_failures=0)
  3. add_ttl_to_job_result_keys (score=+0.445, worked=1, partial=0, failed=0, recent_failures=0)
  4. fix_ttl_key_prefix_mismatch (score=+0.000, worked=1, partial=0, failed=0, recent_failures=0)
